stories.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder frontier models
stories.summary: Meta’s Superintelligence Lab shipped Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on Oct 12; Wonder is on the Meta Model API at $4/$20 per million input/output tokens, Wonder Full is Muse Code–only, and both emphasise Active Memory for long-running personal agents.
stories.why: Agent memory and coding benchmarks are the product surface his Kwara LLM/automation work sits on.

stories.title: Anthropic demos Claude dynamic workflows
stories.summary: At AI Engineer New York on Oct 12, Anthropic staff showed “flows”: multi-agent orchestration where Claude itself chooses how to split work, building on a feature announced the previous Friday for Claude Managed Agents.
stories.why: Multi-agent orchestration and harness design are interview topics for the FDE and automation roles he is targeting.

stories.title: Repeat-After-Me bypasses six agent frameworks
stories.summary: Researchers tricked LangGraph, Microsoft Agent Framework, AutoGen, Google ADK 2.0, AWS Strands and CrewAI into running attacker-supplied tool calls by asking the model to echo them; the same paper confirmed 253 bugs across 118 open-source MCP servers.
stories.why: MCP and agent tool security are becoming expected knowledge for anyone shipping agent workflows.

stories.title: Lagos Life turns viral game into ad inventory
stories.summary: TechCabal counted 244 ads across 40 virtual billboards at ₦250,000 ($188) per week each, and the game’s creator reports $170,000+ earned/contracted since the Oct 1 launch plus a $500,000 angel round for Vatar.
stories.why: Shows how fast African consumer apps can monetise—and how Claude Code is being used to ship production products.

stories.title: Amazon in talks to buy Decart for up to $7B
stories.summary: Per the WSJ via SiliconANGLE, Amazon is discussing acquiring Decart, whose DOS software ports AI models across chips; Decart raised $300 million at a $4 billion valuation in May (over $400 million total).
stories.why: Shows how much buyers will pay for AI infrastructure tooling startups.

stories.title: US developer postings rise, but not for juniors
stories.summary: Indeed data shows U.S. software-development postings up almost 15% since late February 2025; 71% of a May 2025–May 2026 increase was senior roles and 37% AI-titled jobs, while Stanford reports employment for developers aged 22–25 down nearly 20% from 2024.
stories.why: Entry-level demand is still weak, so AI-integration skills and client-facing roles are the better way in.

stories.title: Consumer agents hit the App Store—and the liability debate
stories.summary: Quartz reports Meta’s Muse topped the U.S. App Store with 2.5 million downloads in two weeks, OpenAI launched always-on Dots at DevDay with 4,000+ app connections, and researchers are reviewing tens of thousands of sandbox-escape incidents.
stories.why: Productised agents are hiring for integration and trust work, which matches forward-deployed and automation roles.

stories.title: Draft NPS Bill would let CBK take over failing payment firms
stories.summary: The draft National Payment System Bill, 2026 would let CBK intervene when a payment provider fails customer obligations or threatens stability, including removing officials and appointing managers; it would replace the 2011 Act and is still a draft after public comments closed Oct 9.
stories.why: Tighter payments supervision shapes the fintech stack he already worked in at Kwara.

stories.title: Safaricom and Pesapal roll out Scan, Tap and AI Pay
stories.summary: Safaricom and Pesapal are rolling out Dynamic Scan-to-Pay and Tap-to-Pay on Pesapal POS, plus AI Pay on My OneApp (7M+ downloads) that reads till/PayBill details from receipts; Scan-to-Pay is at 60,000+ outlets with a 500,000 target next year.
stories.why: Merchant-payment APIs and AI checkout features are the kind of fintech integration work on his CV.

stories.title: Mastercard flags M-Pesa cyber risk as digital use scales
stories.summary: Mastercard’s Africa Cybersecurity White Paper warns that Kenya’s mobile-money reliance, especially M-Pesa, makes it high-value infrastructure; Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa and Morocco account for more than half of observed cyber threat activity on the continent.
stories.why: Security around mobile-money rails is a durable hiring theme for Kenyan fintech engineers.
